transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah, hi. Um… I guess the main thing is my focus has gotten kind of unreliable lately. I’m a software developer, and I’ll be fixing something, like a rendering bug, and then a Slack notification comes in—or I notice some color pattern on the screen, or even a siren outside—and suddenly my brain is off on a totally different idea before I’ve even finished the line of code.

It’s not like I’m trying to be careless or anything. I can usually manage pretty well, but lately it’s been… harder to keep my mind on one thing. Does that make sense?
When you were a child, did you also have trouble staying focused?

Not really as a kid, at least not that I remember. I mean, I could get distracted like anyone, but this particular thing feels more recent. It’s been going on maybe about three months—since my platform got selected for the Glendale showcase. That’s when I started noticing it more. Does that answer what you mean?
Since this started, have you had a period where you felt unusually energetic or wired?

Yeah… I mean, I wouldn’t want to overstate it, but yes, kind of. It’s felt like I’ve been running on this constant current. I wake up already thinking through features, exhibition layouts, press angles, code changes… like my brain is already halfway into the day.

And sitting still feels… honestly, it feels like wasting the moment, like I should be using the energy while it’s there. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During this time, have you been needing less sleep than usual?

I’m… not totally sure, to be honest. I don’t think I’ve been tracking it closely enough to say. I mean, there have been nights where I stay up later because I’m working or thinking, but I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is.

I guess I’d have to think about what my normal sleep has been lately. Is that okay?
During this period, have you felt more confident or capable than usual?

I mean… yes, I think so. I don’t want it to sound arrogant, because I know that’s not a great look, but I have felt unusually sure that I’m the person who can pull this together.

Like, the generative art side, the Mexican visual traditions, and the tech community here… I honestly feel like I’m the only one who can connect those in a way that could really change how the city sees public art. Is that the kind of confidence you’re asking about?
Have you been more talkative than usual lately?

Probably, yeah. I mean, I don’t think I’m just talking for no reason, but when I start explaining the platform, I can kind of… keep going.

Like I’ll start with the architecture, then the funding idea, then the cultural impact, then how we’d deploy it, and I realize I’ve been talking for a while. A couple people have said they can’t really get a word in. To me it feels more like the thoughts are coming in too fast to stop cleanly, if that makes sense.
Lately, have your thoughts been racing?

Yeah… I think that’s probably fair to say. I wouldn’t say it feels out of control exactly, but when I start explaining the platform, my mind jumps from the architecture to the funding to the cultural impact to the deployment plan, and it’s like each part is right there waiting.

People have told me they can’t really get a word in, which I guess is a sign. From my side it just feels like the thoughts are arriving too fast for me to pause cleanly. Does that make sense?
Have you been more driven than usual to start or work on projects lately?

Yeah… I’ve definitely been more, um, activated around it, I guess. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m being irresponsible or anything, but the project has started feeling bigger than just something I do outside my regular job.

I’ve been emailing curators, pitching ideas to community leaders, rewriting parts of the backend, sketching out installation plans… and trying to pull in other developers when I can. Sometimes it’s at odd hours, but it feels productive, like I’m finally seeing the whole thing clearly.

Is that the kind of “driven” you mean?
During this time, have you done anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?

A little, maybe. I wouldn’t call it reckless exactly, but… there were a couple decisions I made faster than I probably should have.

I spent some money we hadn’t really agreed on — GPUs, print materials, a promo video, things like that — because it felt like if I waited, we’d miss the window. And I did push an update without getting the usual approval first. At the time, another review cycle just felt like letting the whole opportunity die.

I know that probably doesn’t sound great. I’m not trying to hide it — I just thought I was being decisive, I guess.
Lately, have you been able to function well on much less sleep than usual?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had nights where I stayed up later because I was working on things, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m functioning “well” on less sleep.

I haven’t really been tracking it closely. I probably feel more able to push through than usual, but I don’t want to overstate it. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking?
During this period, have you felt rested after only a few hours of sleep?

I don’t know that I’d say “rested,” exactly. There have been mornings after not much sleep where I got up and kind of went straight into things, and I didn’t feel as wiped out as I would’ve expected.

But rested… I’m not sure. Maybe more like keyed up or able to keep going, if that makes sense. I don’t want to exaggerate it.
Have you been hospitalized because of these symptoms?

No, I haven’t been hospitalized for it. I mean, things have been… stressful, and I know I probably haven’t handled everything perfectly, but it hasn’t gotten to the point where I was admitted anywhere.
Have you had a belief lately that other people would find unrealistic or impossible because of how special, powerful, or important you felt?

I mean… I wouldn’t want to say it sounds impossible, exactly. But I have had this feeling that maybe I’m the person who can put some things together that other people aren’t seeing.

Like, generative art, Mexican visual traditions, and the tech community here — I honestly feel like I might be the only one who can connect those in a way that could really change how the city sees public art. I know that probably sounds a little grand when I say it out loud, but… it feels important to me.
During this period, have you actually felt unusually happy or euphoric?

Yeah… I think so, at least in a way. “Euphoric” sounds a little dramatic, but most days I’ve felt really lit up, like I’m finally in sync with everything and Glendale is catching up to what I’ve been trying to build.

I wouldn’t say I’m just happy all the time, though. If my wife or people at work start slowing things down with, you know, “process” or too many steps, I can get pretty sharp with them. I know that’s not ideal. But underneath it, there’s been this feeling like I’m on, like I can do a lot and shouldn’t be held back. Does that answer what you mean?
How many days in a row has this energized, lit-up period lasted?

Um… if I’m being honest, it’s been more than just a few days. I guess around three months now, since my platform got selected for the Glendale showcase.

I know that sounds like a long stretch, but it hasn’t felt bad exactly — more like I’ve been really engaged and moving with a lot of purpose. Is that the kind of timeframe you mean?
Because of this energized period, have you had serious problems functioning at work or at home?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’ve completely fallen apart or anything. I’m still trying to handle things. But, yes, there have been some real consequences.

Work put me on leave after I bypassed the usual approvals and pushed some changes myself. At the time it felt like I was just getting something important done without all the bottlenecks, but… I can see how that looked to them.

And at home, my wife has been pretty upset. She says the spending and the arguments have made things feel unstable. I don’t like admitting that, but I guess that counts as problems functioning, right?
